title: Justin Welsh: Build a business from a bleeding-neck problem, marketing, and an offer
summary: Justin Welsh explains how he left his job with runway, a pre-built pipeline and intact relationships, and what a business needs: a deeply understood painful problem, a way to get attention, and a differentiated offer. He also shares how he tracks his business (visitors to intended page) and a customer-research action step.

principles.text: A business needs three things: a painful problem, a way to get attention, and a differentiated offer. Two of three is a hobby.
principles.quote: If you have those three things, deeply understanding your bleeding neck problem of your audience, having a a a unique and differentiating way to solve that problem, and then being able to talk about that and get attention for it. If you can do those three things, you have a business.

principles.text: Target a 'bleeding neck' problem: one so painful people pay today. Dig past surface problems to the dollar and emotional cost.
principles.quote: you have to find a problem in your target audience that people are willing to pay for today because it is so painful to solve

principles.text: Painful problems usually involve saving time, making or saving money, being accepted, or improving relationships.
principles.quote: generally it relates to saving time, making money or saving money, being accepted, right? Or improving relationships.

principles.text: If it doesn't keep customers up at night, it isn't a bleeding neck problem. Frame the problem in their concrete stakes.
principles.quote: Nobody goes to bed and can't sleep having nightmares about better team communication.

principles.text: Track visitors to the intended place (the offer or signup page) as the key KPI, since it predicts sales.
principles.quote: the best key performance indicator for my business is simply visitors to intended place.

principles.text: Before going solo: save runway, build pipeline first, leave without burning bridges, and have a risk plan.
principles.quote: I built my runway and I built my business, you know, going out on a limb with a risk reduction plan. So like if this fails then this, if this fails, then this.
